description:
FILED s420, found by the companion re/ leg.

t/re/pat.t reports C: 0/0 with `crash:sb-c::input-error-in-load: read error
during load` — and it is not a PCL parse failure at all: the emitted CL is
4493 lines of correct-looking code containing FOURTEEN byte sequences that are
not valid UTF-8, e.g. for

    like("\x{4000000}", $pat, "...")

PCL emits the character raw, and perl's encoder writes 0x4000000 as the
pre-2003 six-byte extended form (fc 84 80 80 80 80).  SBCL's UTF-8 reader
rejects it with a STREAM-DECODING-ERROR at the first buffer that contains one,
so NOTHING in the file loads: perl gets 1263 passing rows there, PCL gets 0.

SBCL cannot hold such a character at all (char-code-limit is #x110000), so the
value is genuinely unrepresentable — but losing the whole FILE to it is the
#138 failure mode at maximum scale.  The fix is to keep the file READABLE and
make only the offending expression fail:

  * scan string literals at emission for a codepoint >= char-code-limit;
  * emit a form that READS and DIES ON EVALUATION, naming the codepoint and
    citing docs/not-supported.md (the row fails honestly, its file runs);
  * a not-supported.md entry under the Unicode section.

Measure afterwards: re/pat.t is the prize (1263 perl rows), and the same scan
should be run over both populations to find the other files it silently costs.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
DONE s422 (2026-08-22, Opus).  Branch worktree-agent-a970c089570c5ce46.

FIX.  `Pl/ExprToCL.pm`'s `_cl_string_literal_form` -- the ONE writer of a CL
string literal -- already split surrogates and U+FFFE/U+FFFF out of a literal
as `(string (code-char N))` parts of a `(concatenate 'string ...)`.  Its
bad-character class now covers everything above U+10FFFF as well, and such a
part becomes `(p-unrepresentable-char N)`: a form that READS and dies when
evaluated.  `$BAD_CHAR_RE` and `$SAFE_CHARS` are exact complements over the
whole code-point range (verified point by point).  Runtime: exported
`p-unrepresentable-char`, routed through the rule-12 family's
`%p-unsupported-value` (which gained the `&optional detail` its announce twin
already had; it had NO other caller, so the runtime change cannot move
anything).  Message, trappable by `eval { }`:

  PCL: string literal: code point 0x4000000 is not implemented -- above
  SBCL's char-code-limit (U+10FFFF); see docs/not-supported.md "Code points
  above U+10FFFF (perl's extended UTF-8)"

RULE 11: the '...', q{}, q// and s///-replacement paths were four private
copies of the same escaping and now call the one writer.  That closed a hole
the task text did not name -- `s/b/\x{4000000}/` broke the file through its
OWN path (gen_substitution_form wrote qq{"$s"} directly).

NOT A DEFAULT ANSWER: `chr(N)` at run time still yields U+FFFD (the blessed
s318 sec.11 ruling).  The asymmetry is deliberate -- a literal is a
compile-time fact -- and is guarded in both directions in
`Pl/t/wide-codepoint-01.t` and stated in `not-supported.md`.  It is the one
ask of `docs/opus5-review-requests-s422.md` sec.4.

MEASURED.  Gate 156/5622 (only the 13 pclxs xs rows).  corpus-diff IDENTICAL
(111 files, silent drops 7 unchanged).  emission-ab over perl's t/ + lib/ +
cpan-tests (1029 files): SAME 1027, DIFF exactly re/pat.t and
uni/variables.t.  Full sweep --jobs 3: GATE clean, TOTAL 18364 (+0), drops
7 = census.  Population scan of all four corpora (1205 files): only TWO files
decode such a code point into a literal -- t/re/pat.t (8) and
t/uni/variables.t (1); perl-tests/, lib/ and the CPAN dists have none.

THE PRIZE IS NOT COLLECTED, AND WHY IS FILED AS #424.  re/pat.t now LOADS
(the `sb-c::input-error-in-load` signature is gone) but exhausts SBCL's
DEFAULT 1 GB dynamic space mid-run and produces no TAP; with a
measurement-only `--dynamic-space-size 3072` it gives 225/140 and then a
`Failed to match` die.  Raising the heap is a runner decision (PCLSbcl builds
all five command lines, shared memory budget) -> #424.  uni/variables.t does
not move (1248/319 on an a2ac578 worktree and after -- it dies on
`unbound:$}` before the reader reaches the literal's form).
perl-suite-run.tsv spliced ROW BY ROW: pat.t's signature only, with the
cause.

Also filed: #425 (a >U+10FFFF code point in a PATTERN leaks cl-ppcre's own
warning instead of a PCL announce; values agree with perl in every probed
shape).

WHAT NOT TO RETRY: do not add the rule to a quote-form branch -- there is one
writer and the other four paths route through it.  Do not "fix" `chr(N)` to
die to match the literal without re-doing op/chr.t's XDIFF registration.
title: One >0x10FFFF codepoint in a literal makes the WHOLE emitted file unreadable (re/pat.t: 1263 rows)
